newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak FinMin raises '97 budget deficit estimate.
newsitem.headline: Slovak FinMin raises '97 budget deficit estimate.

text.p: The Slovak finance ministry on Tuesday presented the cabinet with a revised 1997 draft state budget, increasing the planned deficit by some seven billion crowns to 36.9 billion, a ministry spokesman said.

"The proposed draft for 1997 state budget plans revenues at 170 billion crowns and expenditures at 206.9 billion crowns, so the overall deficit should total 36.9 billion," ministry spokesman Jozef Mach told a news conference.
Cabinet is expected to approve the budget draft later on Tuesday, so that it could be presented to parliament for final approval by November 15.
"But the government is still discussing the draft and many things can be changed," Mach said, declining to elaborate.
He did not say what items had been added to the revised deficit forecast.
The final draft is the third version of the state budget proposal. The two previous drafts planned deficits of 25 and 30 billion crowns respectively.
Mach said the ministry's budget proposal was based on the assumption that gross domestic product (GDP) will grow at least six percent in 1997 and that inflation would be kept at under six percent.
GDP is expected to total some 660 billion crowns in 1997.
The 1996 state budget deficit is planned to total 27 billion crowns.
Slovakia's state budget deficit totalled 13.4 billion crowns for the January-September period, up from a 7.9 billion crown shortfall for the first eight months of 1996.

Some 25 billion crowns of the planned deficit for 1997 are to be used to service the country's debt, which means that according to IMF standards the 1997 fiscal deficit should total only some 11.658 billion crowns, representing 1.8 percent of the forecast GDP, Mach said.
In 1996, the fiscal deficit calculated according to IMF standards is planned to total some 14.4 billion crowns, or 2.5 percent of the GDP.
